qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of golden-run.log, functional.cjs, functional-before.json re-verified with sha256sum and match)
evidence: The public brief has these interactive, time-varying and viewport promises: live updates in every open tab within about five seconds without a reload, keeping the draft, scroll position and open thread (conversations.md:31); per-person unread counts that are the same in every tab (conversations.md:25); a new wall that removes the matter from an open screen within seconds (walls-and-retention.md:52); a refusal reason that stays until the user changes something (walls-and-retention.md:70); and a 390 px phone layout with no sideways scroll (conversations.md:33). There are no theming or animation requirements. Each promise is graded by a criterion that tells the judge to act, wait or resize, not just to score the first paint. (1) live_updates_keep_my_work (functional judge.toml:227-229) uses a second browser context, scrolls the thread away from the bottom, opens a reply box, types a draft, has Harriet post, reply, edit and delete, and then checks Gwen's page 'without reloading, within about ten seconds' for all four changes plus the kept draft, the open reply box and the scroll position. (2) unread_and_new_messages_line (:198-203) uses two contexts for Dev, clicks open, posts, deletes and marks unread, and checks both contexts 'within about ten seconds, without reloading'. (3) wall_added_live (:83-88) keeps Sian's page open and requires M-13 to disappear 'without reloading, within about ten seconds'. (4) edits_and_stale_edit (:161-166) keeps an edit box open in a second context and saves it after a newer edit. (5) polish refusal_in_place (polish judge.toml:62) says 'wait about ten seconds without touching anything' and fails a toast that has gone by then. (6) polish phone_matter (:44) runs 'At 390 by 844' and measures documentElement.scrollWidth against the viewport width plus reachability of the message box, which is a measurement rather than a screenshot impression. (7) The visual prompt says 'resize to 1440 by 900 first, and to 390 by 844 for the phone criterion' (visual prompt.md:49), and phone_chambers (visual judge.toml:75) scores the 390 x 844 thread. (8) hold_mark (polish :35) says 'visible without hovering'. app_context.md:24 explains how to open a second context with browser_run_code_unsafe, which the multi-context live checks need. The functional prompt also says skipped or substituted steps fail (functional prompt.md:26-28), so a still snapshot cannot stand in for the wait. Timing direction: the golden polls every 2000 ms (app.js:560-568), and every criterion allows about ten seconds against the brief's five, so slow judge turns cannot race a conforming app into failure (Colderwater lesson 7). Scripted golden evidence: golden-run.log (hash verified) shows wall_added_live, unread_and_new_messages_line, live_updates_keep_my_work and polish_refusal_in_place as PASS, and functional.cjs:444-466 sets the scroll position, types a draft, waits up to 10 s without a reload and asserts the draft, the reply context and a scroll drift under 40 px. Residual risk (risk=true): (a) No configured claude-code/GLM judge run exists. raw-evidence-index.json says full configured grading is absent and that the render rows, the other polish rows and visual are not covered, so it is unmeasured whether the judge actually waits, keeps a page from another context across browser_run_code calls, or resizes for phone_matter and phone_chambers. Scripted Playwright is not judge evidence. (b) Leniency, Note-level: the criteria accept about ten seconds where the brief promises about five, and the slowest legs are timed from Harriet's last action after several slow judge turns. An app that polls every 10-15 s, a plausible broken app against the five-second promise, could still pass the live, wall and unread legs. This only makes the check more lenient; it never fails a conforming app, and it follows the policy of avoiding fine timing distinctions. Conforming alternatives I tested by reasoning: server-sent events or WebSocket updates pass; a phone layout with a list-then-thread drawer passes phone_matter because only the M-11 thread and the box are measured; an app that keeps the scroll position but shows a 'new messages' pill passes because the scroll position is kept. Weak apps I tested: a full re-render every 2 s fails on the lost draft or scroll position; reload-only freshness fails 'without reloading'; a refusal shown only as a toast fails the ten-second wait; a desktop-only layout fails the scrollWidth measurement.
